title: JobPutParams
description:
`job.put`'s params (7.6). It creates or replaces the job by `job_id`, idempotently,
and returns `{job_id}` (`job-ref.json`).

```json
{"job_id": "slack-digest", "type": "run", "schedule": {"every_minutes": 15},
 "run": {"kind": "widget_refresh", "prompt": "…", "mount": {"kind": "no_tools"},
         "space": "default"},
 "catch_up": "once", "enabled": true, "loud": false}
{"job_id": "ci-green", "type": "watch", "schedule": {"every_minutes": 5},
 "connector": "claude.ai GitHub", "tool": "mcp__claude_ai_GitHub__get_check_runs",
 "input": {"ref": "main"}, "catch_up": "skip", "enabled": true}
```

rlxd refuses, by error code: `kind_mount_mismatch` and `pinned_call_required` for a
template `run.start` would refuse; `invalid_params` for anything else, an unknown
field, a cron expression it can't read, a time zone it doesn't know, or a watch job's
tool that isn't its connector's included.

catch_up.description: What it does about fires it couldn't make.

connector.description: A `watch` job's connector, such as `claude.ai GitHub`. Required for `watch`.

enabled.description: Whether it fires at all. Absent: `true`.

input.description:
A `watch` job's tool input, a JSON object: the call is pinned to its RFC 8785
SHA-256. Required for `watch`.

loud.description:
Opaque to rlxd: stored, and echoed on `job.fired` and on the fired run's
`run.done` and `run.needs_you`. Absent: `false`.

run.description: A `run` job's template. Required for `run`, refused for `watch`.

tool.description:
A `watch` job's tool, one of its connector's, such as
`mcp__claude_ai_GitHub__get_check_runs`. Required for `watch`.

CatchUp.description:
What a job does about fires it couldn't make (no app connected, rlxd down): `once`
fires once when it can, `skip` waits for the next scheduled time.

oneOf.description: Wait for the next scheduled time.

JobId.description:
A job's id, which the app picks: 1 to 128 ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` and
`:`, starting with a letter or a digit.

oneOf.description: Each fire is a run of the job's `run` template.
Each fire is one pinned read call, with no prompt.

Mount.description:
Which tools a run may reach (7.5).

- `{"kind": "no_tools"}`: none. rlxd passes `--tools "" --strict-mcp-config`, so
  neither built-in tools nor connectors are mounted.
- `{"kind": "connectors", "connectors": ["claude.ai Slack"]}`: built-in tools are
  dropped (`--tools ""`); the gate (5.1) decides which connector tools may be called.

oneOf.description: Only these connectors' tools, each call decided by the gate.

connectors.description:
The connectors, by the name `system/init` gives them, such as `claude.ai
Slack`.

NeedsYouWhen.description:
When a finished run is `needs_you` rather than `done` (7.5): its final output, read at
`pointer`, equals `equals`. The question is read at `question_pointer`. The output is
`structured_output` when the run has one, else the result's text read as JSON.

equals.description: The value there that means the run needs the user.

pointer.description: A JSON pointer (RFC 6901) into the output, such as `/status`.

question_pointer.description: A JSON pointer to the question to show, such as `/question`.

PinnedCall.description: The one call a `send_executor` or `watch` run may make (5.1).

input_sha256.description: The SHA-256, in lower-case hex, of the call's input as RFC 8785 canonical JSON.

RunKind.description:
What a run is for (7.5). Each kind has its own pool, and rlxd's gate rules for it
(5.1).

oneOf.description: A task the user asked for. The only kind whose session persists by default.
Sends one pinned call. Never resumed: a send is never retried.
One pinned read call for a scheduled watch.

RunTemplate.title: RunTemplate
RunTemplate.description: A run job's template: run.start's params (run-start.json) without run_id, which rlxd picks for each fire.

append_system_prompt.description: Text appended to Claude Code's system prompt (`--append-system-prompt`).

deadline_ms.description:
How long the gate waits for the app's answer to each tool call, in milliseconds
(5.1). The hook's own timeout is this plus 10 s.

mount.description: Which tools the run may reach.

needs_connectors.description:
The connectors that must be `connected` before the first turn (5.5): rlxd makes
up to 3 tries, and ends the run `run.failed {reason: "connectors"}` when they run
out, or at once when one is `needs-auth` or `failed`.

needs_you_when.description: When the finished run is `needs_you` rather than `done`.

output_schema.description:
A JSON Schema the final output must match (`--json-schema`); `run.done` then
carries `structured_output`.

partial.description:
Stream partial text as it comes (`--include-partial-messages`): `run.text` events
with `partial: true`.

persist_session.description:
Whether Claude Code keeps the session, so the run can be resumed. Absent: `true`
for a `task`, `false` for every other kind (`--no-session-persistence`).

pinned_call.description: The one call a `send_executor` or `watch` run may make. `null` is none.

prompt.description: The prompt, sent as the run's first stream-json user message.

space.description: The space the run works in (`space.ensure`). Absent: `default`.

timeout_s.description:
End the run `failed {reason: "timeout"}` once its process has run this many
seconds. Absent: no limit.

Schedule.description:
When a job fires: every so many minutes, measured from `job.put` (never drifting with
how late a fire ran), or at each match of a five-field cron expression in an IANA time
zone.

cron.description:
Minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week: `*`, numbers, lists,
ranges, steps, and month and day names.

tz.description: An IANA time zone, such as `UTC` or `Europe/London`.
